issues.claim: Missed subject: `looks`' new `field`, read by V09 and not by V10. R5-08 (c) gave §11.2's `looks` a `field?: Id` (l. 16337–16338), so `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` says whether a famine look draws that field bare (l. 16385). V09 reads it for a field's why card: §4.21.12 (4) (l. 3652–3656) asks `query({ kind: 'looks', view, field })` and adds the `facts` row `info.crisis.ruinedFor` (§5.8; §1b row 377; T-V9-85's 'the why card of a bare field carries `info.crisis.ruinedFor`'). It then says 'Volume 10's explanation renders the same keys (one key, one sentence, J-V9.79)'. V10's read has no field: `read_map` `look` takes `building?: Ref` only (§2.12 l. 954); `over` is 'with the read's building' (§2.13 l. 1023–1025); §3.5 passes only the input's `building` (l. 1458); §1.2 restates `looks` as asked with a building (l. 189); §3.9b (8) tells only 'A house under a disaster look' (l. 2046); row 34 makes a field passed as `building` answer no `over`. At TOWN to METROPOLIS a field's `why` carries no famine row (V07 §4.5's `VillageField` row serves the village rungs only), and the card's `facts` row is the card's own read, not in the `WhyAnswer` that Ask the assistant sends (V09 §5.8). So for 'why is this field bare?' under a famine, the card names the famine on that field and the clerk cannot tell whether it bares it. That is two units with two outcomes for one case (item 122 (f)), and an input the clerk needs has no producer. R5-08's sweep extended V10 only for the building and the section week.
issues.required_change: V10. (1) §2.12's `read_map` union: `| { kind: 'look'; building?: Ref }` → `| { kind: 'look'; building?: Ref; field?: Ref }`; the comment adds '; with `field`, whether each famine look draws that field bare (§11.2's `looks` member's `field`; §10.2 (d)'s `fields`, (f))'. (2) §2.13's `LookAnswer.crises.looks[].over` comment adds '; with the read's field: `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` — whether this famine look draws that field bare at the drawn week (§10.2 (d)'s `fields`, (f)), evaluated in the generation worker; absent where the read's field names no field (V10 §3.23 row 34)'; the projection comment 'and, with a building, over' → 'and, with a building or a field, over'. (3) §3.5 (l. 1458): after '… and no look carries `over`; V10 §3.23 row 34)' add 'and with its `field` where it names a field (one that names none is not passed)'. (4) §1.2's §11.2 row (l. 189): 'asked with a building each disaster look's `over`' adds 'and with a field each famine look's `over`'. (5) §3.9b (8) adds after *A house under a disaster look*: '*A field under a famine look.* "Why is this field bare?" on a field a famine look draws bare (the look read asked with it answering `over` true; V09 §4.21.12 (4)): the field's own state from its `why`, then the look in the why card's words — `info.crisis.ruinedFor` in V09 §4.21.12 (4)'s form — the bare field leaving with the condition; with `over` false (a field the famine leaves sown), the field's own state alone. At THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the village `WhyProvider`'s row (V07 §4.5) tells it, the read adding none.' (6) Row 34: the edges add 'a read asked with a field — one a famine look draws bare, one it leaves sown; a `field` that names no field (a building, a plot or a district, or a field gone since the read that returned it)'; the outcomes add '`over` true on the famine look, the field told as V09's card tells it; `over` false; `over` absent on every look, every other field as without `field`'. (7) T-V10-52 adds 'on V08 §7.1's famine fixture (T-V9-85's, a famine at severity 0.5), "why is this field bare?" on a bare field names the famine in `info.crisis.ruinedFor`'s form, as its why card's `facts` row does, and on a field left sown names none'; T-V10-50's clause (33) adds the `field` forms.

issues.claim: A picture with V09's 'pins and public notes' on has no defined drawing for a public note. `ExportOpts.pins` (l. 16273–16274) draws '§9.5's annotation layer — the view pins and public notes (§2.9; V09 §4.19), drawn as the view draws them'. The view draws public notes only in panels: V09's entity table (l. 4164) has 'pins as markers with their colour; notes in panels', and V09 §4.19 (l. 2905) puts a public note on a thing's About tab and in the Notes panel. §9.5's *Annotation layer* (l. 15118–15119) names only 'the view pins' ('numbered markers and a separate legend sheet'). So a note's drawing is open. One builder draws no note, since the view draws none on the map. Another draws a numbered marker at the noted thing with its text on the legend sheet, §9.5's form. A third draws the text on the map. V09 §5.10 (l. 4064) offers the option by that name. T-ER-19 (l. 16851) runs view pins only, so no bar tells the builds apart. This is an edge on a normal path (a picture of an annotated map) with no defined outcome, built two ways. The round-5 fix carried round 4's wording 'drawn as the view draws them' without saying how a note draws.
issues.required_change: (1) §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins` comment: '§9.5's annotation layer — the view pins and public notes (§2.9; V09 §4.19), drawn as the view draws them, above the map as the furniture is' → '§9.5's annotation layer — the view pins and the public notes (§2.9; V09 §4.19) — above the map as the furniture is: each view pin a numbered marker in its colour at its point, each public note a numbered marker at its thing's anchor as §8.2's Find pins place one (a building's footprint pole of inaccessibility, an area's anchor, a point thing's point), their numbers keyed on §9.5's separate legend sheet to the pin's label and note and to the public note's text; a public note on a thing the export's knowledge withholds left out (§11.1 *Knowledge*)'; the rest stands. (2) §9.5's *Annotation layer*: 'the view pins, §2.9; V09 §4.19 — in a picture only with `ExportOpts.pins`, §11.2' → 'the view pins and public notes, §2.9; V09 §4.19 — in a picture only with `ExportOpts.pins`, each a numbered marker keyed on the legend sheet, §11.2'. (3) END at V09's entity table (l. 4164): 'notes in panels' adds '; in a picture with the Picture tab's **pins and public notes** on, each public note a numbered marker at its thing, its text on the legend sheet (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`; §9.5)'. (4) T-ER-19: the input 'a picture of a map holding view pins with `pins` absent and with `pins` true' adds 'and holding a public note on a building and one on a building the export's key withholds'; the outcome 'no annotation drawn, then every pin drawn' adds 'and the first note's numbered marker at its building with its text on the legend sheet, the withheld building's note left out'.

issues.claim: §8.2 restates the crisis Show's framing narrower than its home in V09. §8.2 *The layer* (l. 13182–13185, written this round from VV910-r4-02 as R5-08 amended it) says 'a preview, drawn alone, carries no condition, so its **Show** frames every crisis mark' and 'V09 §4.21.12 (5)'s **Show** and Find's **Go to** on a look read them so, asking the provider … for one look's marks … and framing their box'. That is one rule for every look. V09 §4.21.12 (5) (l. 3663–3670), the home of the card's Show, frames 'the box of the marks … or for a `disaster` look the union of its units' `FindArea` shapes (V01 §5.4 (6)), or the town's own frame where nothing is drawn for it'. (7) frames Go to 'as the card's Show does' (l. 3677–3678). T-V9-85 runs 'a previewed `disaster` look's Show framing the union of its units' `FindArea` shapes' and 'a look with no mark drawn for it framing the town'. The two rules differ in two cases. (a) A standing disaster whose rebuild has begun in some units: a unit's `ruinTone` stands only 'while the look stands over any of its buildings' (§8.2 l. 13164–13165), so the marks' box shrinks as units hand over (V06 §3.22 (3)), while V09 frames every unit of the look (`LooksAnswer.crises[].districts`). (b) A look with nothing drawn: §8.2 frames an empty box, V09 the town. T-V9-85's disaster clause is a preview, which never hands over, so a Show built from §8.2 passes every bar. That is two units with two outcomes for one case.
issues.required_change: (1) §8.2 *The layer*: '— a preview, drawn alone, carries no condition, so its **Show** frames every crisis mark —' → '— a preview, drawn alone, carries no condition, so its marks are every crisis mark drawn —'. (2) §8.2 *The layer*: 'V09 §4.21.12 (5)'s **Show** and Find's **Go to** on a look read them so, asking the provider in the generation worker for one look's marks at its row's `band` over the map's `bounds` and §8.8's ring, whatever the view, and framing their box.' → 'V09 §4.21.12 (5)'s **Show** and Find's **Go to** on a look read them so, asking the provider in the generation worker for one look's marks at its row's `band` over the map's `bounds` and §8.8's ring, whatever the view, and frame by V09 §4.21.12 (5)'s rule (the box of those marks; a `disaster` look the union of its units' `FindArea` shapes; the town's own frame where nothing is drawn for the look).' (3) END at V09's T-V9-85: add 'on T-V3-40's fixture (T-V9-86's) with the rebuild begun on every building of one of the disaster's units, the standing look's **Show** and Find's **Go to** framing the union of all its units' `FindArea` shapes, that unit's among them'.

issues.claim: Missed subject: `setLayer` and the drawing-group switches, shared by V01, determinism, rendering, V09 and pipeline. Two units switch 'layers' the event cannot carry and no unit defines. V01 §5.1.3 (l. 3039–3041): '**Layer toggles** (T12's `setLayer`; NG F1): the hood pins, model pins and access symbols belong to the `pins` layer and block trees to the `trees` layer, so the view bar hides them'. V01's T12 `dress` bullet (l. 2776–2777): 'its layer toggles (`setLayer`) hide the hood pins with the `pins` layer and the block trees with the `trees` layer'. V01's toggles table (l. 2626) lists 'the `pins` and `trees` layers', and V04 (l. 2780) draws an access head by 'the `pins` toggle'. The base's §4.9 (l. 7946) says 'trees are a layer toggle'. But §7.1's event is `{ t: 'setLayer'; layer: Layer; spec: Partial<LayerSpec> }` (l. 10347), with `Layer` one of underground, ground or sky (§2.1 l. 548). §2.1's wording rule (l. 553–556) says 'the toggleable drawing groups of §8–§9 (labels, cadastral outlines, trees, annotations …) are display-list groups selected by `semantic`, never a fourth model layer'. Nothing defines how such a group is switched: `StyleSheet` (§8.2 l. 12544–12566) has no group switch, §2.9's view keys have none, §8.4's *Toggles are visibility* covers only `LayerSpec.visible`, V09's T12 `dress` row (l. 1739) takes V01's `pinGate` and vignette but offers no pins or trees switch, and `agreement.json` lists `setLayer` only between V09 and V10. So a builder of V01's toggle must either extend `Layer`, against §2.1, or invent a mechanism (logged style state, or a per-viewer view key). Two builders then differ in whether hiding the trees is undoable, shared and saved, and V09's builder offers no control. This is an interface with callers and no implementer (principle (7)).
issues.required_change: Rendering, with ENDs; the style form is chosen because V01 lists the switch beside the style's `details` and `shadows`, which are style state. (1) §8.2's `StyleSheet` adds `groups: { trees: boolean; pins: boolean };   // the drawing groups a T12 `dress` switch hides (§2.1's wording): `trees` every tree instance and block tree (§8.10; V01 §5.1.3's block-tree slot), `pins` every model pin, hood pin and ground-access symbol (V01 §5.1.3's slot 10); default true; set by a logged `setStyle` (§7.4's row: style state, outside the model digest, undone as a style edit); a picture draws what the style draws`. (2) §8.4's *Toggles are visibility* adds '; a drawing group (§2.1) is switched by `StyleSheet.groups` (§8.2), a logged `setStyle`, never by `setLayer`'. (3) END at model §2.1: 'are display-list groups selected by `semantic`, never a fourth model layer' adds '— trees and pins switched by `StyleSheet.groups` (§8.2)'. (4) END at pipeline §4.9 (l. 7946): 'trees are a layer toggle' → 'trees are a drawing-group switch (`StyleSheet.groups.trees`, §8.2)'. (5) END at V01: §5.1.3's '**Layer toggles** (T12's `setLayer`; NG F1): the hood pins, model pins and access symbols belong to the `pins` layer and block trees to the `trees` layer' → '**Group switches** (T12's `setStyle` of `StyleSheet.groups`, §8.2; NG F1): the hood pins, model pins and access symbols belong to the `pins` group and block trees to the `trees` group', and 'the `pins` toggle' → 'the `pins` switch'; the T12 bullet's 'its layer toggles (`setLayer`) hide the hood pins with the `pins` layer and the block trees with the `trees` layer' → 'its group switches (`setStyle` of `StyleSheet.groups`, §8.2) hide the hood pins with `pins` and the block trees with `trees`'; the toggles table's 'the `pins` and `trees` layers' → 'the `pins` and `trees` group switches (`StyleSheet.groups`)'. (6) END at V04 (l. 2780): 'the `pins` toggle' → 'the `pins` switch (`StyleSheet.groups.pins`, §8.2)'. (7) END at V09's T12 `dress` row (l. 1739): 'V01 (pinGate, vignette)' adds '; the Dress panel's **Trees** and **Pins** switches (`setStyle` of `StyleSheet.groups`, §8.2)'. (8) The test that runs V01's toggles-table row runs each switch: hidden, logged as one `setStyle`, undone, and the document's model digest unchanged.

issues.claim: repair-r5-V09's HAND-OFFS ask V10: 'V10's explanation of a building under a previewed `disaster` renders `info.crisis.ruinedForPreview` (V09 §4.21.12 (4); T-V9-86)'. V09 §4.21.12 (4) makes the why card's `facts` row for a building a disaster look stands over `info.crisis.ruinedFor` 'in the form the line takes' (`ruinedForOpen`, `ruinedForUnnamed`, `ruinedForUnnamedOpen`, under a preview `ruinedForPreview`), and says volume 10 'renders the same keys'. V10 names no `ruinedFor` key: `LookAnswer.looks[].says` carries the legend's line forms only (l. 1015); §3.9b (8)'s *A house under a disaster look* (l. 2046–2051) quotes 'for now its quarter is drawn burned: the Great Fire, weeks 12–20' with no key; C10 says only that the clerk 'tells the drawn ruin as the look's'. The hand-off is not closed at its destination. It is minor: the clerk reads the same look, condition and weeks, and only the catalogue key its sentence renders is unnamed.
issues.required_change: V10. (2) C10's outcome 'the clerk tells the drawn ruin as the look's' adds '(`info.crisis.ruinedFor` in its form, V09 §4.21.12 (4))'.
